body:
Seems to be some kind of dependency version problem...
Anyway in JBang to see the dependency tree that was used?

@geoand I'm not quite sure if this is the right way to produce a dependency tree but my approach was

1. start in editing mode with `jbang edit --open=code --live quarkusapp.java`
2. open a terminal inside the editor / IDE
3. run `gradle -q dependencies > deps.txt`

Probably every other editor / IDE will do it.

[The deps.txt file produced is attached](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/files/8487407/deps.txt).
My question was more towards @maxandersen who is the creator of jbang :)

Run with jbang --verbose and it will show classpath. 

'jbang info tools app.java' should also list it.

Btw. The issue is probably that the example does not use the bom (we should update it to use that) but it's weird that reactive resteasy as the top dependency does not work out of the box. 

That indicates something wrong/weird in its default dependency chain.

> Btw. The issue is probably that the example does not use the bom (we should update it to use that) but it's weird that reactive resteasy as the top dependency does not work out of the box.

Very good point! Adding the BOM fixes the issue. So I'll update the docs to include the BOM

issue.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

JBang offers commands to retrieve a list dependencies; e.g. `jbang info tools <appfile.java>`, `jbang --verbose`

Using these approaches, the full path of dependencies in the file system is exposed. When having to share dependency information for troubleshooting it would be convenient to be able to share such information without revealing details on the host system.

For automated comparison a simple list is a good option. For human understanding a tree structure can be advantageous.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

`jbang info dependencies <appfile.java>` defaults to a tree representing the dependencies (GAV); no path information

E.g.

```
\--- io.quarkus:quarkus-resteasy:2.8.0.Final
     +--- io.quarkus:quarkus-vertx-http:2.8.0.Final
     |    +--- io.quarkus:quarkus-core:2.8.0.Final
```

`jbang info dependencies --list <appfile.java>` outputs a simple list with each GAV line by line; no path information

E.g.
```
io.quarkus:quarkus-resteasy:2.8.0.Final
io.quarkus:quarkus-vertx-http:2.8.0.Final
io.quarkus:quarkus-core:2.8.0.Final
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

1. open script in IDE
2. launch terminal in IDE
3. show dependencies using Gradle 

**Additional context**

see https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/24926
